reason: TypeScript 7 removed moduleResolution node10; resolving as bundler follows package.json exports, so a dual package's ESM types (.d.mts) win over the CommonJS ones TypeScript 6 picked (.d.ts)
TypeScript 7 prints a function with properties assigned to it (Grid.Item = ...) as an object type with a call signature; TypeScript 6 prints typeof Grid
TypeScript 7 no longer treats ES5 constructor functions in JavaScript (function F() { this.x = 1 }) as classes: F is a plain function
As js-constructor-functions: new F() on a constructor function is any in TypeScript 7, an instance of class F in TypeScript 6
TypeScript 7 types a CommonJS module's exports as the object assigned to module.exports; TypeScript 6 as typeof import("<file>")
TypeScript 7 resolves `module` and `exports` in CommonJS files to the module and exports objects; TypeScript 6 to the synthetic export= symbol
TypeScript 7 no longer declares members from this.x = ... assignments inside JavaScript constructor functions, so those members and calls through them are any
TypeScript 7 no longer adds an implicit ...args: any[] parameter to JavaScript functions that read `arguments`
For a property read through an index signature (process.env.X), typescript-go returns the index signature's symbol; TypeScript 6 returns none
